title: SpatialArena Benchmark Tests 52 3D Models, Feed-Forward Wins
summary: New SpatialArena benchmark evaluates 52 geometric foundation models across five 3D tasks. Feed-forward models now outperform specialist depth networks.
body_markdown:
#### 💡 TL;DR


- SpatialArena benchmark evaluates 52 geometric foundation models across five 3D perception tasks using 23 public datasets plus 30 new LiDAR-grounded scenes.
- Feed-forward 3D and 4D models now outperform specialized monocular depth networks, with VGGT-Omega leading MonoDepth, VideoDepth and SfM rankings.
- Single-image depth approaches saturation on public benchmarks at 4.9% AbsRel but jumps to 14.2% on harder real-world captures.


A comprehensive new benchmark released this week reveals a fundamental shift in 3D perception: general-purpose feed-forward models are now outperforming specialized depth estimation networks. SpatialArena, published on Hugging Face, evaluates 52 geometric foundation models across five 3D tasks and 23 datasets totaling 418,929 images, plus a held-out suite of 30 scenes with 32,655 LiDAR-grounded images.


The findings challenge the conventional wisdom that task-specific architectures hold an edge in depth prediction. Feed-forward 3D and 4D models not only match monocular specialists on public benchmarks but surpass them on real-world captures, while halving the error of the best dedicated video depth model.


## Release date and availability


Officially released on November 25, 2026, SpatialArena is now available as an open benchmark on Hugging Face. The platform includes evaluation code, dataset access, and a live leaderboard tracking the 52 models tested across MonoDepth, VideoDepth, Structure-from-Motion, and 3D vision-language tasks.


## Feed-forward models dominate leaderboard


VGGT-Omega, a[feed-forward network](https://emergent.sh/glossary/feed-forward-network) , claims first place across MonoDepth, VideoDepth, and SfM categories. The benchmark data shows feed-forward 3D/4D models improving at 8.4 points per year on MonoDepth tasks, while monocular specialists decline 2.8 points annually. On video depth tasks, the gap is even more dramatic: feed-forward approaches deliver half the error of the best dedicated video depth architecture.


The paper documents a clear performance divergence. Best monocular depth models achieve 4.9% absolute relative error on public datasets but climb to 14.2% on SpatialArena's harder, uncontrolled captures. By contrast, VGGT-Omega posts 6.5% versus 14.0% for specialists, maintaining a consistent advantage across both benchmark types.


## Monocular depth approaches saturation


Single-image depth estimation shows signs of maturity on established benchmarks. The research team reports that best monocular AbsRel improved only from 5.5% to 4.9% over two years on public datasets. Yet on SpatialArena's 30 new scenes, errors reach 14.2%, versus 2.4-8.0% across the 23 public collections, indicating significant headroom remains on real-world data.


Current depth networks reveal predictable failure modes. Models calibrate to a 1-5 meter range and compress distant structure. The benchmark also exposes a gravity-aligned prior: networks predict depth roughly twice as accurately on upright front-facing cameras compared to rolled side-camera angles, suggesting they have not learned rotation-invariant[3D reconstruction](https://emergent.sh/glossary/3d-reconstruction) .


## Benchmark design and dataset scale


SpatialArena's evaluation suite spans five core 3D perception tasks:


- Monocular depth estimation on single images
- Video depth prediction across temporal sequences
- Structure-from-Motion camera pose and sparse point clouds
- 3D vision-language model reasoning
- Multi-view geometry consistency checks


The benchmark contributes 30 original scenes with 32,655 LiDAR-grounded images, achieving 98.3% pixel-level agreement within ±25% AbsRel. This dataset complements the 23 public collections, covering indoor, outdoor, automotive, and robotic scenarios. The researchers also evaluate large vision models including Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Astra, and Gemini 4 Argon on 3D VLM tasks, extending the benchmark beyond geometric methods into multimodal reasoning.


## What this means for 3D perception


SpatialArena's core finding is blunt: no single model leads on every dataset, indicating the field has not yet converged on a unified architecture for 3D structure. The benchmark establishes that general[foundation models](https://emergent.sh/glossary/foundation-model) trained on diverse 3D data now absorb the capabilities of narrower depth specialists. For practitioners, this suggests feed-forward 3D architectures offer a more robust starting point than monocular depth networks, particularly for applications involving varied camera angles, long-range scenes, or temporal sequences. The 14.2% AbsRel ceiling on new captures also signals that real-world deployment still requires significant error margins beyond public benchmark performance.
